elements.scope_reason: Red-box criterion: pallor AND any of (pulse >= 100, RR >= 30, dizziness, weakness, chest pain). Six parts.
elements.problem: Logic is right: (and Pallor (or pulse>=100 RR>=30 Dizziness Asthenia Chest pain)) matches the page's "Pallor with ... or ..." reading, and all six parts are present with correct thresholds, directions and the only available rate unit (bpm). Two concept problems. (1) Pulse >= 100 is measured on "Pulse, function" (8499008), whose parent is "Cardiovascular function": it names a physiological function, not a rate. The measurable observable is "Heart rate" (364075005, parent "Cardiovascular measure"). If the routine pulse vital is recorded under Heart rate this comparison never matches, and the pulse part of the criterion is silently lost. (2) Pallor is encoded as "Pallor of skin of face" (1209208002), which narrows the page's generic "pallor" (in APC usually conjunctival/palmar pallor) to the face; "Pale discoloration of entire skin of body" is the other candidate and SNOMED has no plain "Pallor" finding, so this is a lesser concern but should be noted. "Asthenia" for weakness and the routine "Respiratory rate" concept are acceptable.

rule_level_problems.problem: Pulse >= 100 is compared on (measurement "Pulse, function" bpm). "Pulse, function" (8499008) is a cardiovascular-function observable, not a rate; "Heart rate" (364075005) is the measurable. If the routine pulse vital is not recorded under this concept the comparison never matches and the pulse arm of the pallor criterion is silently lost.

Footnote 1 defines "shock likely" (SBP < 80, pulse >= 100, RR > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness) and the red box cites it. The house standard says a red-box criterion backed by an "X likely" gets a probable rule referenced via (active_condition X). Instead Shock is a bare tickable finding and confusion/restlessness is not checked for at all.
